Executive Order 14330 directed Labor to reconsider alternative-asset guidance and possible safe harbors; it did not automatically add private credit to a specific plan.
DOL proposed process-based safe harbors and required fiduciary consideration of performance, fees, liquidity, valuation, benchmarks and complexity.
SEC alleged more than 1.9 billion dollars raised through ABS and double pledging; allegations are not final adjudications.
OTIC reported estimated tender requests equal to 38.1 percent of shares and quarterly liquidity up to 5 percent, while stating ordinary repayments covered repurchases.
Federal Reserve research documents rapid growth in bank lending to private-credit vehicles and potential stability channels; the video's exact 13-versus-4 percent statement was not reproduced.
On-time payoff can help, but a high balance at calculation time may affect a score even when paid in full the next day.
Score direction depends on the entire file; reported balances can lag; closure and paid-off loans can affect utilization or credit mix without fixed point effects.
A limit decrease may raise utilization, while the resulting score may fall, rise or remain unchanged; closed accounts can continue to affect history length.
Applications commonly create hard inquiries that can affect scores; prescreening, account reviews and self-review are soft inquiries that do not.
Negative payment information is generally reportable for seven years and positive history may remain after closure; this does not prove selective retention after authorized-user removal.
In a 1,001-person study, one in four identified possible score-affecting errors, but about 5 percent had errors that could affect credit terms; no current 40-million estimate follows directly.
CFPB alleged faulty dispute intake, failure to convey information and improper reinsertion; allegations are not final adjudications.
CFPB ordered Equifax to pay a 15 million dollar civil penalty for improper dispute investigations.
FHFA approved FICO 10T and VantageScore 4.0 for future Enterprise use; implementation details changed after the video's publication.
Long-term net-capital-gain rates depend on taxable income and asset type; short-term gains use ordinary rates.
FDIC's April 2026 table reports a 0.38 percent national savings rate.
The table records 4.03 percent for November 2025-April 2026 issues and 4.26 percent for the May-October 2026 earning period.
A qualifying REIT must distribute at least 90 percent of taxable income; distributions and returns remain exposed to investment risks.
BLS reports a 1204 dollar 2025 median weekly earnings value for full-time wage and salary workers; the script's roughly 1000 dollar value is stale and not an all-worker average.

BLS 2021 consumer-unit means exactly reproduce the script's 66928 total, 22624 housing, 8289 food and 10961 transportation figures; they were stale by the 2025 upload and are not medians or required take-home income.
About 28 percent of non-retired adults reported no retirement savings; this is not all Americans and does not prove reliance entirely on Social Security.
SSA reports an average 1975.34 dollar monthly retired-worker benefit in December 2024, materially above the script's stale 1550 dollar amount.
Experian reports average FICO 715 and average credit-card balance 6730; supports the score but not a 9000 dollar household-debt claim.
Gallup's 2025 retiree sample reported mean actual retirement age 62; nearby years report 61. It is a retiree survey mean, not an administrative all-American statistic.

Strategy disclosed a June 29 program for up to 1.25 billion dollars of Bitcoin-sale proceeds for its USD Reserve and said all capacity remained available on July 5.
MARA disclosed about 1.5 billion dollars of Q1 Bitcoin sales used to retire debt and reduce a credit line; this supports one miner's liquidity-driven selling, not an industry aggregate.

BIP-361 proposes phased migration and restrictions with rescue-protocol concepts; it is not adopted code or a settled confiscation of exposed-key coins.
